sentences.text: What if this famous vampire is really just a kiss?
This is Love and Pain, painted by Edvard Munch in 1895.
Everyone knows it by another name, Vampire.
The critic Stanisław Przybyszewski saw a submissive man with a biting vampire's face on his neck.
And the picture seems to agree.
Her red hair pours over him, and her arms hold him tight.
There are no teeth, no blood.
According to Munch himself, it showed nothing more than a woman kissing a man on the neck.
The name Vampire came from his friend, never from Munch.
He still painted the embrace six times in three years.
It's love, and the pain that comes with it.
So is she biting him, or holding on to him?

meta.title: Munch said his vampire was only a kiss
meta.description: Love and Pain was painted by Edvard Munch in 1895 and is better known as Vampire, a name given by the critic Stanisław Przybyszewski. Munch always said it showed nothing more than a woman kissing a man on the neck.
